entry.title: [Pillow] Pillow: Memory disclosure and segfault in libtiff encoder via crafted TIFF tags
entry.content:
============================================================================
Memory disclosure and segfault in libtiff encoder via crafted TIFF tags
Location: src/encode.c:1014  in PyImaging_LibTiffEncoderNew()
Commit:   a707c6b21c313880d0771e54965d142dd42358b6
============================================================================

A crafted TIFF file of a few hundred bytes makes Pillow copy an attacker-chosen amount of its own process memory into the TIFF it writes back out, or crash the process outright. The trigger is an ordinary Image.open() followed by a bare im.save(fp, "TIFF"). The only precondition is that the application re-saves images as TIFF. When the uploaded file is compressed, Pillow routes that save through libtiff automatically, with no options from the application. The attached reproducer does this with a 356-byte LZW TIFF: one crafted tag comes back holding 65536 bytes taken from _imaging.so's read-only data, and a second crafted tag makes the worker die with SIGSEGV on every run.

The bug is in PyImaging_LibTiffEncoderNew (src/encode.c). It decides what arguments to pass to the variadic TIFFSetField() from the shape of the Python value (scalar, tuple or bytes). It assumes its ImagingLibTiffMergeFieldInfo() call defined how libtiff will read them. But TIFFMergeFieldInfo() never overrides libtiff's built-in field table, so libtiff reads the arguments according to its own definition of the tag:

  • For a counted array tag such as DNGPrivateData (50740), a count-1 integer in the source file is taken as the byte count. The data pointer is then read from an argument slot Pillow never wrote, and that many bytes are copied into the output.
  • For a fixed-size array tag such as ActiveArea (50829), the integer itself is used as the source address.

Where that unwritten slot points depends on the compiler. In the tested clang build it points into _imaging.so, and a larger count returned thousands of pointers into libpython, libc and libtiff, which defeats address-space randomisation for anyone chaining another bug. When the application preserves metadata with tiffinfo=im.tag_v2, a 64-bit entry turns ActiveArea into a 16-byte read from an address the attacker chooses. All observed memory errors are reads; no out-of-bounds write was found.

Other branches of the same loop share the defect and are reachable from crafted TIFFs or from EXIF in JPEG/PNG/WebP re-saved as compressed TIFF. These are the bytes, RATIONAL-tuple and typed-tuple branches, and a BYTE-typed ColorMap. The file-reachable forwarding was introduced in a3d45e9cefd0 ("Added custom int and float TIFF tags") and first released in 5.4.0.

Details

PyImaging_LibTiffEncoderNew (src/encode.c:777-1060) chooses the argument list it hands to the variadic TIFFSetField() from the Python value of each tag — scalar vs. tuple vs. bytes, and a type that is either autodetected or copied from the source file's IFD — and assumes that its own ImagingLibTiffMergeFieldInfo() registration defines how libtiff will read the va_list. It does not: libtiff keeps its built-in definition for every tag it already knows, and core tags are never registered at all. libtiff therefore consumes the varargs as (count, pointer), (pointer) or three pointers according to its field table, whatever Pillow actually pushed. The encoder never consults that table (TIFFFindField / TIFFFieldPassCount / TIFFFieldWriteCount / TIFFFieldDataType) before the call.

The most severe instance, and the one the attached reproducer exercises: when a TIFF is re-saved through the libtiff writer, every tag of the source IFD that Pillow does not recognise is forwarded to libtiff with TIFFSetField(). A count-1 integer entry is passed as a single scalar vararg. If libtiff's own field table defines that tag number as an array field, libtiff consumes the varargs as (count, pointer) or (pointer) instead, so the attacker's integer becomes either the number of bytes to copy from a never-written vararg slot, or the source address itself. The same mismatch is reachable through the typed tuple branches (tuple length consumed as a pointer for fixed-count built-in tags such as CFARepeatPatternDim, even when the source file is well-formed), the bytes, TIFF_RATIONAL-tuple and core-tag branches of the same loop; those are listed under Other branches with the same defect below and need to be covered by the same fix.

A 181-byte TIFF (16×16 RGB, one LZW strip, plus one extra IFD entry 50740 / LONG / count 1 / value 4096 — DNGPrivateData) opened with Image.open() and saved with a bare im.save(buf, "TIFF") produces a 4296-byte output whose tag 50740 holds 4096 bytes that occur nowhere in the input; scanning /proc/self/mem finds them in the read-only data segment of _imaging.so. Changing the extra entry to 50829 / LONG / 1 / 64 (ActiveArea) makes the same two calls segfault in memcpy(dst, src=0x40, n=16) under ImagingLibTiffSetField ← PyImaging_LibTiffEncoderNew. An ASan build of the extensions reports READ of size 4096 in memcpy called from src/encode.c:1014 for the first input.

Code path

_save copies all tags of the opened image into the libtiff attribute list. For a tag that is neither in LIBTIFF_CORE nor in TiffTags.TAGS_V2, no type is recorded, so the value goes through untyped:

# src/PIL/TiffImagePlugin.py:1782
supplied_tags = {**legacy_ifd, **getattr(im, "tag_v2", {})}
…
# :1959-1982
for tag, value in itertools.chain(ifd.items(), supplied_tags.items()):
    if tag not in TiffTags.LIBTIFF_CORE:
        …
        elif isinstance(value, (int, float, str, bytes)) or …:
            type = TiffTags.lookup(tag).type      # None for 50740, 50829, …
            if type:
                types[tag] = type
    if tag not in atts and tag not in blocklist:
        …
            atts[tag] = value                     # plain int 4096

compression defaults to the source image's im.info["compression"] (TiffImagePlugin.py:1731-1746), so a compressed source selects the libtiff writer without the application asking for it.

In the encoder the untyped int is autodetected as TIFF_LONG (src/encode.c:805-815), the tag is "registered" as a scalar custom field, and then set with one 32-bit vararg:

// src/encode.c:844      (is_var_length = 0 → writecount 1, passcount 0)
if (ImagingLibTiffMergeFieldInfo(&encoder->state, type, key_int, is_var_length)) {
    … continue;
}
…
// src/encode.c:1013-1016
} else if (type == TIFF_LONG || type == TIFF_IFD) {
    status = ImagingLibTiffSetField(
        &encoder->state, (ttag_t)key_int, (UINT32)PyLong_AsLong(value)
    );

The registration does not do what the caller assumes. TIFFMergeFieldInfo() only adds definitions for tags libtiff does not already know and returns 0 (success) either way, so for tags in libtiff's built-in table the built-in definition stays in force. Queried against the linked libtiff 4.5.0 after exactly Pillow's merge call:

50740 DNGPrivateData      type=BYTE   passcount=1 writecount=-1   (unchanged)
50829 ActiveArea          type=LONG   passcount=0 writecount=4    (unchanged)
65000 CustomField         type=LONG   passcount=0 writecount=1    (Pillow's definition, tag was unknown)

libtiff's setter for FIELD_CUSTOM tags then interprets the va_list according to its definition: for passcount=1 it reads va_arg(ap, int) as the element count — the attacker's 4096 — allocates count * size bytes and memcpys that many bytes from va_arg(ap, void *), a slot PyImaging_LibTiffEncoderNew never wrote. On x86-64 that slot is register rcx; in this build it holds a pointer into _imaging.so's .rodata, so the copy succeeds deterministically (a value of 2 000 000 also succeeds and yields a 2 000 200-byte output). TIFFWriteDirectory writes the copied bytes into the output file as the tag's value. For fixed-count array fields (passcount=0, writecount=4 for ActiveArea) there is no count argument, so the attacker's scalar is consumed as the void * source and 16 bytes are read from address 64 → SIGSEGV.

Tags in libtiff 4.5's built-in table that Pillow forwards untyped and that take the (count, pointer) form include DNGPrivateData 50740, CFAPattern 33422, CFAPlaneColor 50710, LinearizationTable 50712, BlackLevel 50714, WhiteLevel 50717, ColorMatrix1/2 50721/50722, AsShotNeutral 50728, OriginalRawFileName/Data 50827/50828, AsShotICCProfile 50831, CurrentICCProfile 50833. Fixed-count ones (pointer only → crash) include ActiveArea 50829, DNGVersion/DNGBackwardVersion 50706/50707, DefaultScale/DefaultCropOrigin/DefaultCropSize 50718–50720, AsShotWhiteXY 50729, CFARepeatPatternDim 33421, BlackLevelRepeatDim 50713, ImageLayer 34732, RawDataUniqueID 50781.

When the application saves with tiffinfo=im.tag_v2 (the documented way to preserve metadata), the file-declared type is honoured, and a LONG8 entry reaches the (uint64_t)PyLong_AsLongLong(value) branch at src/encode.c:1049-1052. For ActiveArea that is a 16-byte read from a full 64-bit attacker-chosen address into the output: a source entry 50829 / LONG8 / 1 / <address of a Python bytes object> produced an output ActiveArea of (b'SECR', b'ET-T', b'OKEN', b'-012') in testing.

The comment above blocklist += at TiffImagePlugin.py:1938-1944 already notes that array tags with the wrong length "will result in segfaults"; the blocklist covers only a handful of tags Pillow itself knows, not the ones libtiff knows and Pillow does not. Forwarding of these tags was introduced in a3d45e9cefd0 ("Added custom int and float TIFF tags", 2018-10-25), first released in 5.4.0; releases 2.0.0–3.0.0 forwarded them as scalars too, until 9fa6634f4 ("Partial fix for #1597") limited _save to LIBTIFF_CORE.

Other branches with the same defect

The scalar-integer branch above is one of several places in the same loop where the call shape is derived from the Python value rather than from libtiff's definition. All of the following were confirmed on this commit (stock build crashes and/or ASan reports, stack always memcpy ← libtiff ← ImagingLibTiffSetField src/libImaging/TiffDecode.c:934 ← PyImaging_LibTiffEncoderNew), and all are reachable from a sub-1 KB crafted file followed by an ordinary save():

  • Typed tuple → (len, av) for a fixed-count built-in field (src/encode.c:904-994, the SHORT/LONG/SBYTE/SSHORT/SLONG/FLOAT/DOUBLE tuple branches all call ImagingLibTiffSetField(..., len, av)). For libtiff built-in fields with passcount=0 and a fixed writecount — CFARepeatPatternDim 33421 (SHORT×2), BlackLevelRepeatDim 50713 (SHORT×2), ImageLayer 34732 (LONG×2), ActiveArea 50829 (LONG×4), MatrixWorldToScreen/Camera 33305/33306 (FLOAT×16) — libtiff takes the first vararg as the source pointer, so the tuple length becomes the memcpy source address. A perfectly well-formed 206-byte 8×8 PackBits TIFF carrying 33421 / SHORT / 2 / (2, 2) re-saved with a bare im.save(out, "TIFF") dies with SIGSEGV in memcpy (gdb: rsi = 0x2, the tuple length) on every run; so does Image.new("L", (8, 8)).save(buf, "TIFF", compression="packbits", tiffinfo={33421: (2, 2)}), and a JPEG whose EXIF carries the tag saved with exif=im.getexif() into a compressed TIFF. bytes values for built-in fixed-count BYTE tags (e.g. DNGVersion 50706, BYTE×4) crash the same way through the (PyBytes_Size, PyBytes_AsString) call at src/encode.c:860-865. The mirror image for passcount=1 fields: Photoshop 34377 declared SHORT, count 1, value 60000 takes the scalar branch at :1009-1012, libtiff reads 60000 as the count and an unpassed vararg as the pointer, and the re-save succeeds with a 60162-byte output whose tag 34377 holds 60000 bytes of process memory (here C prototype strings from _imaging.so's .rodata).
  • bytes value → single char * (src/encode.c:805-815 autodetects bytes as TIFF_ASCII; :1033-1042 passes PyBytes_AsString(value) alone). ImageFileDirectory_v2._setitem stores a BYTE-typed entry as bare bytes and an ASCII-typed one as str (encoded to bytes by _save), so the file's declared type selects this branch.
    • ColorMap (320) declared BYTE with 4 bytes of data in a non-palette PackBits TIFF: 320 is in core_tags[], no type is consulted, the value skips the 768-tuple TIFFTAG_COLORMAP branch (:871-895) and libtiff reads three uint16_t * and copies 1 << BitsPerSample shorts from each — a 512-byte over-read of the 5-byte Python bytes buffer, then dereference of two stale argument registers → SIGSEGV on every run of Image.open(f); im.save(out, "TIFF"). COLORMAP is not in _save's blocklist.
    • Photoshop (34377) declared ASCII: _save copies value and type (TiffImagePlugin.py:1802-1818; only IPTC_NAA_CHUNK has a BYTE/UNDEFINED type guard there, from commit 2245df0a — PHOTOSHOP_CHUNK and XMP do not). libtiff's definition is BYTE, passcount=1, so the low 32 bits of the char * become the byte count for a memcpy from a stale register (ASan: READ of size 3518384; stock: SIGSEGV in about half of runs, otherwise RuntimeError). Impact

Any service that accepts a TIFF and writes it back out as TIFF through libtiff — which happens with a plain im.save(fp, "TIFF") whenever the uploaded file is compressed, or whenever a compression= other than raw is requested — returns to the uploader, inside one metadata tag of the produced file, an attacker-chosen number of bytes read from a stale pointer in the worker process, deterministically and without retries. Which memory that is depends on the compiler's register allocation for PyImaging_LibTiffEncoderNew: in this clang build the pointer is _imaging.so + 0x1588, so a request for 262 144 bytes (which succeeded every time in testing, as did 2 000 000) covers the extension's .rodata, .data.rel.ro/GOT and .data and returned 2 800+ resolved pointers into libpython, libc, libtiff, libjpeg and others — a complete ASLR bypass for chaining with any other memory bug; a gcc build of the same source left a different, unrelated address in that slot. The fixed-count variant kills the worker process with SIGSEGV from a 181-byte upload on every request. With tiffinfo=im.tag_v2 the source address is fully attacker-chosen (16-byte arbitrary read into the output for ActiveArea, or a crash). No non-default Pillow setting is involved; the only precondition is TIFF-to-TIFF re-encoding.

The other branches add further deterministic process-kill inputs (BYTE-typed ColorMap in any RGB or palette TIFF; thumbnail() keeps tag_v2, so open→thumbnail→save-as-TIFF is affected too) and extend the reach to JPEG/PNG/WebP uploads whose EXIF is preserved with exif= when converting to libtiff-compressed TIFF. All the memory errors are reads; libtiff sizes its destination buffers with the same count it copies, so no out-of-bounds write was found.

Reproducing

repro is one Python script, run against the stock build with the installed PIL. It needs no compiler and no extra files.

upload(tag, value) has Pillow write a 16×16 red RGB image as an LZW-compressed TIFF, then appends a new IFD holding the same entries plus one extra <tag> / LONG / count 1 / value (kept in tag order) and points the header at it — a 356-byte input on this tree. The source is LZW-compressed on purpose. A bare im.save(out, "TIFF") keeps the source's compression, so the save goes through the libtiff writer even though the application passes no arguments. resave() is the whole "application": Image.open(BytesIO(src)); im.save(out, "TIFF").

The script runs three cases:

  1. Control, tag 65000 = 4096. libtiff does not know this tag, so the file is re-saved correctly and the output tag reads back as the integer 4096. This is what should happen to every tag.
  2. Leak, DNGPrivateData 50740 = 65536. libtiff's built-in definition of this tag is a counted BYTE array. It reads Pillow's single scalar as the count and takes the data pointer from a vararg slot Pillow never wrote. The output tag comes back as bytes of length 65536 that do not occur in the input. The script prints the first 32 of them and the file offset at which they occur in _imaging.so on disk. On this build they always do (offset 0x57588): the stale pointer aims into the extension's read-only data.
  3. Wild read, ActiveArea 50829 = 64. libtiff defines this tag as a fixed LONG[4] array with no count, so it uses the scalar 64 as the source address. The script re-runs itself as a child process (repro child, core dumps disabled) to do this re-save, and the child exits with -11, meaning SIGSEGV.

Expected output on the affected tree:

control  tag 65000=4096 -> 4096
leak     tag 50740=65536 from a 356-byte upload -> 65536 bytes not present in input, head a661fcffc661fcff3360fcff7b61fcffd361fcff085ffcffe061fcff3360fcff
         leaked bytes found in _imaging.so at file offset 0x57588
crash    tag 50829=64 -> child exit -11 (SIGSEGV)
BUG

The script prints BUG if case 2 leaks or case 3 crashes. Both are deterministic on this build. A fixed Pillow prints OK: the tag does not come back as 65536 bytes of foreign data (it reads back as None, or save() raises ValueError/RuntimeError, which the script catches), and the child exits with something other than SIGSEGV (0, or 1 if save() raised).

The other branches can be checked by hand on the stock build in the same way (each as Image.open(f); im.save(BytesIO(), "TIFF") in a child process): a PackBits RGB TIFF with an extra IFD entry 320 / BYTE / 4 / "ABCD" → SIGSEGV every run; a PackBits palette TIFF whose ColorMap is 320 / BYTE / 2 saved with tiffinfo=im.tag_v2 → SIGSEGV every run; a Pillow-written JPEG whose EXIF holds tag 50000 = RATIONAL×2 saved with compression="tiff_lzw", exif=im.info["exif"] → SIGSEGV in most runs, RuntimeError ("Failed to allocate memory for custom tag binary object (-N elements of 4 bytes each)") in the rest.

Suggested fix

The encoder must not guess the calling convention; it has to ask libtiff what the tag's effective definition is after ImagingLibTiffMergeFieldInfo and marshal accordingly, or refuse. The attached patch does this for non-core tags:

  • a new ImagingLibTiffFindField() in src/libImaging/TiffDecode.c (declared in TiffDecode.h, next to the other libtiff wrappers) returns libtiff's TIFFFindField type, passcount and writecount for a tag;
  • in PyImaging_LibTiffEncoderNew (src/encode.c), for a non-core tag that libtiff already knows, Pillow adopts libtiff's type when it has none of its own, and after ImagingLibTiffMergeFieldInfo a new tiff_field_matches() checks the value against libtiff's definition: a scalar only for a single-value field whose C argument type (int / uint64_t / double / char *) matches, an array only with libtiff's element size and, for fixed-count fields, exactly writecount elements. Anything else raises ValueError("Tag value does not match libtiff field definition") instead of reaching TIFFSetField — this covers the reproducer's DNGPrivateData and ActiveArea inputs, ASCII-typed Photoshop, short PrimaryChromaticities and the LONG8 tiffinfo= variant;
  • every tuple/bytes branch now goes through set_tiff_array_field(), which passes len only when the field has passcount set; this also fixes the TIFF_RATIONAL branch, which never passed a count (and extends it to TIFF_SRATIONAL);
  • TIFF_UNDEFINED fields are registered as variable-length, matching how their bytes values are passed;
  • Tests/test_file_libtiff.py gains a regression test (scalar DNGPrivateData, scalar and 2-tuple ActiveArea rejected; well-formed values round-trip).

Core tags and tags libtiff does not know keep their current behaviour. With the patch applied to a clean checkout and rebuilt, the reproducer no longer triggers and the test suite passes. It is not a complete fix, however: the whole check sits inside if (!is_core_tag), so the BYTE-typed ColorMap variant stays open. The PackBits RGB TIFF carrying 320 / BYTE / 4, re-saved with a bare save(), no longer segfaults at this point but writes 1536 bytes — over-read from the 5-byte bytes object and two stale varargs, including 22 live heap pointers — into the output ColorMap, which is still a disclosure. Before merging, it needs a guard that accepts TIFFTAG_COLORMAP only through the existing 768-tuple branch, never through the scalar or bytes branches, and ideally the same shape check for the other core tags libtiff special-cases in _TIFFVSetField (YCbCrSubsampling 530, TransferFunction 301, ReferenceBlackWhite 532).

Narrower Python-side mitigations in _save close individual entry points but not the class, and are worth adding alongside the C-side check: drop tags with TiffTags.lookup(tag).type is None from supplied_tags (closes the Image.open()→save() path shown here but not tiffinfo= callers); remove COLORMAP from supplied_tags next to EXIFIFD/SAMPLEFORMAT and extend the IPTC_NAA_CHUNK BYTE/UNDEFINED type guard to PHOTOSHOP_CHUNK and XMP; add 318/319/529 to the blocklist next to REFERENCEBLACKWHITE; and have _save ifd.tagtype.pop(tag, None) before assigning its own ColorMap/BitsPerSample/ICCProfile/… values so a tiffinfo=-imported type cannot reshape them. The C-side check is the fix to rely on.

# Pillow libtiff writer: a count-1 integer tag copied from the source TIFF is passed to
# TIFFSetField() as one scalar vararg; for tags libtiff itself defines as arrays it is
# consumed as a byte COUNT (DNGPrivateData 50740 -> N bytes of process memory written
# into the output) or as a POINTER (ActiveArea 50829 -> SIGSEGV).  Application side is
# the ordinary "open upload, save as TIFF" (compression is inherited -> libtiff writer).
import io, struct, subprocess, sys, resource
from PIL import Image

def upload(tag, value):
    """Pillow-written 16x16 LZW TIFF, plus one extra IFD entry <tag> LONG[1] = value."""
    b = io.BytesIO()
    Image.new("RGB", (16, 16), "red").save(b, "TIFF", compression="tiff_lzw")
    data = bytearray(b.getvalue()); assert data[:4] == b"II*\0"
    (off,) = struct.unpack_from("<I", data, 4)
    (n,) = struct.unpack_from("<H", data, off)
    ents = [bytes(data[off + 2 + 12 * i: off + 14 + 12 * i]) for i in range(n)]
    ents.append(struct.pack("<HHII", tag, 4, 1, value))
    ents.sort(key=lambda e: struct.unpack_from("<H", e)[0])
    data += b"\0" * (len(data) & 1); new_off = len(data)
    data += struct.pack("<H", len(ents)) + b"".join(ents) + struct.pack("<I", 0)
    struct.pack_into("<I", data, 4, new_off)
    return bytes(data)

def resave(src):                       # the whole "service"
    im = Image.open(io.BytesIO(src)); out = io.BytesIO(); im.save(out, "TIFF")
    return out.getvalue()

if len(sys.argv) > 1 and sys.argv[1] == "child":
    resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_CORE, (0, 0))
    resave(upload(50829, 64)); sys.exit(0)

print("PIL core:", Image.core.__file__)
ctl = Image.open(io.BytesIO(resave(upload(65000, 4096)))).tag_v2.get(65000)
print("control  tag 65000=4096 ->", repr(ctl))

N = 65536
src = upload(50740, N)
try:
    v = Image.open(io.BytesIO(resave(src))).tag_v2.get(50740)
except (ValueError, RuntimeError) as e:   # a fixed Pillow may reject the tag

print(f"leak     tag 50740={N} from a {len(src)}-byte upload ->",
      f"{len(v)} bytes not present in input, head {v[:32].hex()}" if leak else repr(v)[:80])

    print("         leaked bytes found in _imaging.so at file offset", hex(so.find(v[:256])))

rc = subprocess.call([sys.executable, __file__, "child"])

entry.title: [compose-lint] compose-lint: Text in a pull request can still issue CI workflow commands through compose-lint 0.31.0's output
entry.content:
Impact

0.31.0 fixed GHSA-6f4g-xm8v-pgv6, where text from a Compose file became GitHub Actions workflow commands in compose-lint's output. The fix escapes the command openers in everything compose-lint prints, and the 0.31.0 changelog says the report "escapes both openers (also covering Azure Pipelines)". Five paths were left open:

  • Unicode whitespace before a line-leading ::. The runner strips all Unicode whitespace from the start of a line before it looks for a command. compose-lint only accounted for spaces and tabs, so a no-break space or another Unicode space ahead of :: is not escaped. It can come from a Compose value, or from a file name: the text report's file heading and per-file summary, and the fix summary on stderr, start with the path as given, so a directory named with a leading no-break space followed by :: puts a command at the start of a line. This reaches those lines, the text report's fix guidance, the fix dry-run diff, and continuation lines of stderr diagnostics.
  • JSON and SARIF printed to stdout. --format json and --format sarif output never passed through the sanitizer, so ##[ inside a service name or other value reaches the log intact when the output isn't redirected to a file.
  • Command-line errors. When a repository path reaches compose-lint's arguments without a -- before it, the argument parser prints it raw in its error message. That includes a carriage return, which the runner treats as a line break, so a command can also start a new line there.
  • Azure Pipelines. ##vso[ logging commands were not escaped on any path, despite the changelog's Azure claim.
  • An error message in the GitHub Action (0.30.0 and 0.31.0). When sarif-file: names a file in a subdirectory that can't be created, the Action prints the directory's resolved path in an error message, outside the window in which it turns command processing off. A pull request can commit a symlink on that path to a directory whose name contains a newline followed by a command. The documented setup, sarif-file: results.sarif at the repository root, is not affected.

A pull request can therefore create annotations, fold or hide parts of the job log, or issue other commands the runner accepts, when CI runs compose-lint over it, before anyone reviews it. The pass/fail result is not changed.

Affected setups are those that print compose-lint's output to a CI log without the GitHub Action: the compose-lint package run directly in a workflow, the pre-commit hook run in CI, and the Docker image. The pre-commit hook is affected in its default configuration: it passes each changed file's path to compose-lint, and a path whose directory name starts with Unicode whitespace and :: reaches the report's file heading. The JSON/SARIF and command-line paths also need output left on stdout, or args: without the documented trailing --, which is why they alone would score lower. The GitHub Action turns command processing off around each compose-lint run, so of these paths only its own error message affects it, and only when sarif-file: points into a subdirectory. That setup is outside the documented one, which is why that path alone would also score lower.

Found during an internal pre-1.0 security review.

Docker image. composelint/compose-lint tag 0.31.0, the matching minor tag, and latest are affected.

Releases before 0.31.0 are covered by GHSA-6f4g-xm8v-pgv6, except the Action's error message, which also affects Action 0.30.0.

Patches

Fixed in 0.32.0. The line-start escaping covers every character the runner strips before ::, so it holds for quoted values and file names alike. JSON and SARIF on stdout escape ##[ inside strings as \u005b, which decodes to the same data. argparse's own messages go through the same sanitizer. ##vso[ is escaped everywhere. In the Action, the SARIF-directory error names the sarif-file: input as written.

Workarounds

  • Upgrade to 0.32.0 or later.
  • On GitHub Actions, use the tmatens/compose-lint Action, or bracket the compose-lint step with ::stop-commands::<random token> and ::<token>::, as the Action does.
  • In the Action, keep sarif-file at the workspace root, for example sarif-file: results.sarif.
  • Write --format json and --format sarif output to a file rather than the log.
  • End the pre-commit hook's args: with --. This closes the command-line path only; it does not stop a file name at the start of a report line, so in CI also bracket the pre-commit step with ::stop-commands:: as above.
  • On Azure Pipelines, don't print compose-lint's output from runs over untrusted pull requests to the job log.

Reproduction

On compose-lint 0.31.0 on a GitHub-hosted runner (runner 2.337.0), each of the following creates an annotation:

  • a Compose file with image: "nginx\n\u00a0::notice::X", linted with the text report;
  • a directory named \u00a0::notice::X (a no-break space, then ::notice::X) holding a compose.yml, linted with compose-lint -- '<that directory>/compose.yml', or by the pre-commit hook in its default configuration;
  • a service named a##[warning]X, linted with --format json or --format sarif to stdout;
  • compose-lint '--##[warning]X/compose.yml' with no --;
  • the Action with sarif-file: out/reports/results.sarif, where out is a committed symlink to a directory named d\n::warning::X that contains a regular file reports.

The same inputs with a plain space in place of the no-break space, or with -- before the path, or with sarif-file at the repository root, create none. The same inputs on compose-lint 0.30.0 create annotations even with a plain space, which is GHSA-6f4g-xm8v-pgv6. The composelint/compose-lint:0.31.0 image produces byte-identical output to the package.

entry.title: [OctoPrint] OctoPrint: Stored XSS via saved connection parameters
entry.content:
Impact

OctoPrint versions 2.0.0rc1 up until version 2.0.0rc6 are susceptible to cross-site scripting via a specially crafted default port or baudrate setting on the bundled Serial Connector plugin, supplied via the API as new defaults during a connect request.

Patches

The vulnerability is patched in 2.0.0rc7.

Workaround

Check config.yaml for Javascript fragments in printerConnection.preferred.parameters.port or printerConnection.preferred.parameters.baudrate. If found, remove them. You can check who of your users had access to your instance since you flashed 2.0.0rc1 or above via auth.log.

Credits

This vulnerability was discovered and responsibly disclosed to OctoPrint by "mahn-don".

entry.title: [compose-lint] compose-lint: Incomplete fix for GHSA-jf3h-8jvx-vcrg: a run stopped at the finding limit quotes a secret from a CI-generated `.env`
entry.content:
Impact

This is an incomplete fix for GHSA-jf3h-8jvx-vcrg. 0.32.0 made findings quote the ${NAME} a sibling .env filled in, instead of its value. The same release added a stop at 20,000 findings per document, and that stop is checked before the quoting step. A run that hits it reports the findings graded so far with the resolved values still in them, in text, JSON and SARIF output. That happens with or without --allow-partial-coverage.

The attack is the one GHSA-jf3h-8jvx-vcrg describes. In a CI workflow that writes secrets into the .env beside the Compose file, a pull request changes a line to image: "${DB_PASSWORD}". It also pushes the document past 20,000 findings, which a few hundred lines can do, because an aliased list is graded once for each service that uses it. The secret's value is quoted in a finding that reaches the job log, the JSON output and the SARIF uploaded to Code Scanning. GitHub masks registered secrets in the job log, but not in uploaded JSON or SARIF artifacts or in Code Scanning alert text. The run exits 2, or 0 with --allow-partial-coverage, after the output has been written.

The preconditions are the same as for GHSA-jf3h-8jvx-vcrg. The workflow writes secrets into the .env beside the Compose file and runs on pull requests from authors who should not see them, such as a pull_request_target workflow that lints the pull request's files. Pull requests from forks normally run without secrets, so the common setup is not exposed. The inflated document is visible in the pull request, but the workflow runs before anyone reviews it.

Found during an internal pre-1.0 security review.

Python package. compose-lint 0.32.0. Earlier releases have no finding limit, and their quoting gap is GHSA-jf3h-8jvx-vcrg itself.

GitHub Action. Action tag v0.32.0 is affected. Tags before v0.22.0 install the newest release unless version: is set, so they currently install 0.32.0.

pre-commit hook. rev: v0.32.0.

Docker image. composelint/compose-lint:0.32.0, :0.32 and latest are affected when the .env is mounted with the project.

Patches

No fixed release yet.

Workarounds

  • Run with --no-env, which skips the sibling .env.
  • Don't write secrets into the .env beside the Compose file in a job that lints untrusted pull requests.

Reproduction

project/.env          DB_PASSWORD=example-secret      (written by CI, not committed)
project/compose.yml   x-p: &p [ ...200 port mappings... ]
                      services: one service with image: "${DB_PASSWORD}" and ports: *p,
                                plus about 100 more services with ports: *p

compose-lint --format sarif compose.yml exits 2 with "grading stopped at 20000 findings", and the reported findings contain example-secret. The same file with fewer services stays under the limit and quotes ${DB_PASSWORD}. Checked against the 0.32.0 wheel from PyPI, using a synthetic value.

entry.title: [gpustack] GPUStack: Missing authorization on several cluster and resource endpoints allows cross-user access and cluster takeover
entry.content:
Impact

An authenticated non-administrative user could access a Kubernetes cluster they are not authorized to access through GPUStack's Kubernetes API proxy.

The cluster_apiserver_proxy handler did not perform a resource-level authorization check before forwarding requests to the selected cluster. Requests were forwarded through a worker using its Kubernetes ServiceAccount credentials.

Depending on the permissions granted to that ServiceAccount, an attacker could read sensitive Kubernetes resources, create or modify workloads, or delete resources and disrupt services. Creating attacker-controlled workloads could result in code execution in the target cluster.

Exploitation requires a Kubernetes-provider cluster with a reachable worker. The operations available to the attacker are limited by the worker's ServiceAccount permissions.

Patches

Fixed in gpustack v2.2.2.

Workarounds

Restrict access to the GPUStack instance to trusted administrator accounts until upgrading.

entry.title: [gpustack] GPUStack: SAML callback trusts an unverified SAMLResponse, allowing authentication bypass and account takeover
entry.content:
Impact

The callback Base64-decodes the posted XML, reads NameID and attributes, resolves or provisions the user, and mints a gpustack_session JWT — but never calls OneLogin_Saml2_Auth.process_response(), the step that verifies the signature, issuer, audience, destination, and time conditions.

No credentials are required, and SAML SSO does not even need to be configured. The callback processes the payload and issues a session regardless of whether SAML is set up, so every deployment is affected, not only SAML-enabled ones. Anyone who can reach the endpoint over the network can authenticate as an arbitrary identity by posting a response that names it:

  • If the name matches an existing user (e.g. an administrator), the attacker receives that user's session — full account takeover, including administrator access.
  • Otherwise, a new non-admin user is provisioned.

Administrator access grants full control over the deployment and the infrastructure it manages. Because Response/Assertion IDs are never consumed, a captured signed response also replays indefinitely.

Precondition: network reachability to /auth/saml/callback. SAML SSO configuration is not required. A full proof-of-concept is available privately to maintainers.

Patches

Fixed in gpustack 2.2.2:

  • The SAML callback now validates the response via OneLogin_Saml2_Auth.process_response() — signature, issuer, audience, destination, and time conditions — and rejects responses that fail, so forged or replayed assertions are no longer accepted.
  • The SAML and OIDC login/callback routes are now gated to run only when that provider is the configured active provider, so a deployment that has not enabled the provider no longer parses attacker-supplied IdP payloads.

Workarounds

There is no effective configuration-level workaround — disabling or not configuring SAML does not mitigate this on affected versions, since the callback runs regardless. Until upgraded, block network access to /auth/saml/callback (e.g. at a reverse proxy / ingress).

Credit

Reported privately by Austin Chu, Sohee Kim, and Corban Villa (UC Berkeley security research project), and independently, earlier, by a researcher who wishes to remain anonymous.
